guarantees.claim: When rst_ni is low (active reset), app_id is cleared to 0 regardless of other inputs.
When clr_appid is high and not in reset, app_id is cleared to 0, overriding set_appid.
When set_appid is high, no reset, and clr_appid is low, app_id is updated to app_id_d.
When no reset, clr_appid, or set_appid condition is true, app_id retains its previous value.
guarantees.cond: none of the above conditions true

assumptions.claim: app_id_d must be a valid application index within the width AppIdxW when set_appid is asserted and not masked by higher-priority conditions.
assumptions.cond: set_appid asserted and not overridden by rst_ni or clr_appid
assumptions.risk: A malformed or out-of-range application index could be latched, potentially selecting an unintended application and compromising access control or key usage.

uncertain_points.claim: The priority of clr_appid over set_appid is fixed by RTL ordering, but it is unclear whether this is always the desired behavior; if both are pulsed together, the clear wins and the set is ignored.
uncertain_points.cond: clr_appid and set_appid simultaneously active, not in reset
uncertain_points.risk: If a higher-level protocol expects the set to take effect even during a clear, the application index may be erroneously zeroed, leading to a No-Application state or wrong operation.

uncertain_points.claim: app_id holds its value indefinitely when no clear or set occurs; there is no mechanism in this block to automatically clear it after an operation completes.
uncertain_points.cond: Last operation finishes, no new set or clear assertion
uncertain_points.risk: A stale application ID may remain selected, enabling an unauthorized application to access cryptographic keys or data in subsequent transactions, violating access control (the comment 'Do not select any' suggests the idle state should be zero).
